summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired confirmatory NetOps study testing constrained prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair (gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a synthetic N=150 intent corpus. Execution artifacts and analysis are archived. Results show a near-ceiling baseline (149/150) with a single guarded repair success (150/150); paired absolute difference = 0.0067, exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]. Authors appropriately bound conclusions to the synthetic corpus and single model and disclose preregistration, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and limitations (single model, synthetic tasks, ceiling effect).
critical_issues: Main manuscript contains run-internal provenance artifacts (file paths and full SHA-256 hashes) and log-level detail embedded in the scientific prose rather than an archival pointer; this violates the track guidance to keep run-internal paths/hashes out of ordinary prose and substantially reads like an artifact report rather than a concise conference paper.

The Disclosure Statement is exhaustive and log-like in places; per the track requirement it should be concise and not duplicate execution logs or execution-manifest-level bookkeeping in the manuscript body. This must be condensed while preserving the mandatory items.
required_revisions: Remove or relocate run-internal file paths and full artifact hashes from the main manuscript text. Replace them with a concise archival pointer (e.g., "full execution bundle and hash manifest archived at [artifact-bundle reference]"), and move all log-level provenance (paths, per-file hashes) into the archived artifact bundle or a supplement. Do not remove the mandatory Disclosure Statement items—only remove low-level run bookkeeping from the narrative.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to the required concise content (LLMs used, model identifiers, orchestration framework, initial master prompt reference, autonomy-lock boundary, preregistration fingerprint, verifier and adapter identifiers, and a brief statement that full logs/artifacts/hashes are archived). Remove duplicated execution-log text and per-file inventories; keep the Disclosure within the five-page manuscript.

Add a short, explicit sentence placed prominently in Methods and repeated in Results that the preregistered constrained-only condition (B) was not executed and that no results or inferences are presented for B (i.e., make the unexecuted preregistered analysis explicit and prominent).
optional_revisions: Replace one small provenance example in the paper body with a single concise, human-readable exemplar task (1–2 lines) to illustrate tasks and failure modes while keeping detailed examples in the archive.

In the Discussion, add a brief prescriptive note recommending a small pilot baseline calibration step when preregistering power assumptions for LLM-for-NetOps trials to avoid ceiling-effect mismatches (can be phrased as methodological guidance rather than additional experiments).

Consider moving a compact evidence-to-claim table or nearest-work comparison (1/2 page) into the main paper if space permits; otherwise ensure clear pointers to the archived artifacts where that table is stored.
